merge_rule: 2-of-3 promotion: a chapter is 'hard' only if >= 2 reviewers flagged it hard. Otherwise soft if >= 1 reviewer flagged it.

reasons: Citations count of 0 is a hard miss -- the meta-chapter that explains how to read the book should reference the chapters it maps to

reasons: Word count 2616 is 784 words below minimum 3400 -- this is a structural completeness problem, not a polish issue (flagged by all 3 reviewers)

Agent definitions loading from ~/.claude/agents is described but the chapter does not address what prevents a malicious agent definition from being loaded (e.g., in a shared workstation or CI environment)
No analysis of how plugin-provided agents differ from user-authored agents in terms of trust and security
The loading sequence is described but error paths (malformed frontmatter, missing fields, conflicting agent names) are not covered
Frontmatter parser is covered but the security implications of loading arbitrary markdown+YAML from disk are not addressed
The chapter does not explain what constitutes a well-structured agent definition versus a poorly-structured one
merged_flags.suggested_angle: Expand to meet minimum word count. Add a section on the trust model for agent definitions (plugin vs user vs built-in agents and what permission isolation each gets). Add error handling paths with concrete examples of malformed vs well-formed agent definitions. Address the supply-chain risk of agent definitions loaded from shared directories.
